text:
Okay, that's up on screen. Four phases left to right, top to bottom.

Phase 1 is Style Identity — the quiz. Starts with an anchor grid that warm-starts a Bayesian prior, then up to 24 pairwise image comparisons that update it, then you confirm your top-3 style blend. That fingerprint is the through-line for everything that follows.

Phase 2 is Capture — budget selection, photo upload where we EXIF-rotate and normalize the image, then Modal runs perception on it: SAM3 over 15 furniture-class prompts to figure out what's in the room and what you want to keep.

Phase 3 is the redesign, and this is the meaty one. Before we ever touch an image, Claude Sonnet acts as a Design Director and produces a structured brief — anchor piece, palette, materials, object hierarchy, LoRA weights. That gets compressed into a 50-to-80-word FLUX prompt by Claude Haiku. Gemini analyzes the room architecture so we don't accidentally redesign your walls. Then it all flows into Modal's 4-pass render engine: Pass 0 is a layout planner, Pass 1 is the heavy creative hit at strength 0.92 with the full LoRA stack, Pass 2 adds surface detail at lower strength, Pass 3 relights the scene with IC-Light, and then there's editorial post-processing and a Claude QA score.

Phase 4 is commerce — Claude Vision reads the render, Serper searches Google Shopping per item, results are budget-filtered and affiliate-tagged, and everything lands in the shoppable shelf.

Happy to zoom into any section.
